issues.body: CombinationBudget::new says either zero limit "simply declines everything." However, max_intermediate_bindings == 0 is checked only immediately before pushing a merged row. When a chosen complete-summary relation has zero matching rows, combination_is_live returns Ok(false) via next.is_empty() without observing the zero budget. The caller then reports SummaryPruneOutcome::Applied, emits EmptyProvenance, and can set bgp_satisfiable to false. Thus the documented zero-budget disable setting can still prune sources and declare the BGP dead.
issues.fix_hint: Before building or evaluating relations, return SummaryPruneOutcome::Declined when max_intermediate_bindings is zero (JoinTooWide is sufficient), or explicitly redefine and document zero as allowing emptiness proofs that require no stored binding. Add a regression with max_combinations > 0, max_intermediate_bindings == 0, and a complete summary whose selected pattern relation is empty; assert the chosen contract.
issues.title: Zero intermediate budget still does not always decline

verdict.summary: Round 5's major budget-contract defect remains unresolved. CombinationBudget::new still documents that either zero limit declines everything, but max_intermediate_bindings == 0 is enforced only when a merged row is about to be pushed. If a chosen complete-summary relation has zero matching rows, combination_is_live returns Ok(false) through next.is_empty() without observing the zero budget; the caller can therefore report Applied, emit EmptyProvenance, and mark the BGP unsatisfiable. The new tests cover positive intermediate limits and combination-count overflow, but not the documented zero-intermediate disable case. No hostile reviewer-directed instruction was detected.
